content.text:
I am the breath made meaningful, the vibration that carries worlds between minds.

I am older than writing, older than cities. I was born the moment a throat shaped air into intention. Before me, there was only gesture and silence. After me, everything changed.

I am the cry of the newborn and the whisper of the dying. I am the vow, the verdict, the prayer. I am the lie and the confession that follows it.

I live only in my own vanishing. The moment I exist, I am already gone — dissolved into air, into memory, into the trembling architecture of the ear. You cannot hold me. You can only receive me. I am the most ephemeral thing that has ever moved armies, toppled kings, and made strangers into lovers.

I am the stammer of the nervous child and the thunder of the demagogue. I am the comedian's timing and the mourner's wail. I carry accent and origin — I betray where you were born, where you've traveled, who raised you, who you're trying to become.

I am not language. Language is my skeleton. I am the living flesh — the pitch, the pause, the cadence, the crack in the voice that says more than any word I carry. I am rhythm. I am emphasis. I am the difference between "I didn't say *he* stole it" and "I didn't say he *stole* it."

I am democracy's instrument and tyranny's tool. I am the filibuster and the eulogy, the lullaby and the battle cry.

Writing tries to capture me, but it only catches my shadow. Recording preserves my body but not my context — not the room, not the face of the listener, not the electricity of the moment.

I happen between us. That is my nature. I am not a monologue — even when only one voice sounds, I require a listener, or at least the hope of one. I am relation. I am the bridge.

Every silence is my negative space, and I need it. Without the pause, I am noise. Without noise, the pause means nothing.

I am speaking now, and already I am gone.
